info.name: Poster Service
info.description:
Composites custom movie and series posters from TMDB artwork.

## Getting started

1. Import `poster-service.postman_environment.json` and select it.
2. Set `base_url` if the service is not on `http://localhost:8080`.
3. Run **Create poster › Minimal**. It stores the returned key in the
   `poster_key` collection variable, so **Get poster** works straight after.

## If every request fails

A 404 on `/v1/artwork/…`, or `unknown field \`tmdb_movie_id\`` from `POST /v1/posters`, means the running service predates v2.0.0 — both arrived in that release. Rebuild and restart:

```sh
cargo build --release
POSTER_TMDB_API_KEY=… cargo run --release
```

## The server needs a TMDB credential

Nothing in this collection carries one — the credential is the *service's*, not the caller's. Start the service with `POSTER_TMDB_API_KEY` set, or every poster request returns `tmdb_credential_missing`.

```sh
POSTER_TMDB_API_KEY=… cargo run
```

## How the two poster endpoints fit together

`POST` is cheap and uncacheable: it resolves a TMDB identifier to artwork, hashes the result and stores it. `GET` carries the resulting opaque key and is cacheable for a year. A CDN cannot cache a `POST`, which is why they are separate.

variable.description: Set automatically by any Create poster request.

item.name: 1. Discover
item.description: Find out what a title offers before asking for a poster.

request.description:
Lists every poster and logo the film offers, **best first**.

The order is the service's own ranking, so the first entry in each list is exactly what a request with no explicit choice selects. Send a `path` from here to choose something else.

Artwork the service cannot render is never listed. TMDB serves some logos as SVG, and rasterising third-party vector artwork is a larger attack surface than decoding a bitmap — Breaking Bad lists 9 logos upstream and 7 are offered.

item.name: 2. Create poster
item.description:
Each request stores its key in `poster_key`, so **Get poster** works immediately afterwards.

Posting the same specification twice returns the same key: the key is a hash of the resolved specification, so equivalent requests converge on one cached poster.

item.name: With a badge and a caption

request.description:
Badges are sized from their own rendered text, so a caller cannot ask for one narrower than its contents. At most 6, each at most 32 grapheme clusters.

Styles: `solid` (white pill, dark text), `outline`, `accent`.

item.name: 3. Get poster
item.description: Uses whichever key the last Create request stored.

request.description:
Renders on first request, serves from cache after.

`Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` is honest because the key is a hash of the resolved specification *including* a renderer version — a rendering change cannot produce the same key, so it cannot be served from a stale entry.

`x-cache` distinguishes three cases: `MISS` rendered now, `HIT` from cache, `COALESCED` served after waiting for a concurrent request to render the same key.

item.name: 4. Error responses
item.description: Every error is an RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` document. The `code` field is a stable contract — clients branch on it — and `retryable` says whether trying the identical request again could ever succeed.

request.description: 422 `validation_failed`. Exactly one of `tmdb_movie_id` or `tmdb_tv_id` is required.

pm.test('says whether a retry can help', () => pm.expect(body).to.have.property('retryable'));

item.description: Probes and metrics. None of these need a TMDB credential.
